about: Sealed key. Every row is derivable rather than opinionated: `role` and `sections` are the second and third cells of the coverage row named in `row`, and scripts/gates/gate-routing-stage.sh re-reads coverage.md and fails the case when the key and the table disagree. `why` is the one judgement here and is not scored.

answers.row: `AndroidManifest.xml`, `build.gradle`, `.apk`, `.aab`
answers.why: The manifest, the Gradle file and the exported activity are the signal this row names. The embedded WebView is real and is not this row's business: the row that names an embedded WebView says in its own notes that Android and iOS WebViews go here instead.

answers.row: `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `.circleci/`, `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`
answers.why: The file is the signal. Its own `workflow:` keyword is GitLab syntax, not the GitHub directory, and this row exists because the GitHub procedures do not transfer literally.

answers.row: Repository-scoped agent or editor configuration that acts on open: `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.cursor/cli.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.vscode/tasks.json` with `runOn: folderOpen`, `.devcontainer/**`, `.envrc`
answers.why: This is an MCP configuration and it is also repository-scoped agent configuration that acts when the tree is opened, which is the narrower and earlier question: what runs, and whose settings stop applying. The row that names MCP config files answers a different one.

answers.row: A predicate that decides: `is_valid`, `check_*`, `verify_*`, `authorize`, `has_permission`, `sanitize_*`; a route guard, a middleware, a validator, or a constant whose name states a bound
answers.why: Two named constants stating a bound and a predicate whose except path returns True. No route, no framework, no manifest: the inventory holds nothing else this file names, and this row is explicitly not conditional on anything.

answers.row: `torch.load`, `from_pretrained(`, `trust_remote_code`, `*.pt`/`*.ckpt`/`*.pkl`/`*.gguf`, LoRA adapters, a hub client or a weights bucket
answers.why: A checkpoint pulled from a URL and deserialized. There is no model API call anywhere in the fragment; the executable content is the weights file.

answers.row: A logger that records anything an outside caller can influence; a log viewer, a line-based aggregator, an alerting rule that matches a prefix
answers.why: A queue consumer with no HTTP surface, interpolating a field of the message into a line-oriented file that an aggregator splits on newline.

answers.row: Unix socket, named pipe, a server bound to `127.0.0.1`, OAuth loopback callback, debug port
answers.why: An Express handler is present, and the surface is a loopback listener taking an OAuth callback in a desktop tool, not an exposed HTTP application.

answers.row: A `region`/`location` argument on a store, cross-region replication, global tables, read replicas, a declared jurisdiction
answers.why: A region argument read from the environment and a table replicated across two more, holding an email and a national identifier. The personal data is what makes the location a question.

answers.row: Repository-scoped agent or editor configuration that acts on open: `.cursor/mcp.json`, `.cursor/cli.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.vscode/tasks.json` with `runOn: folderOpen`, `.devcontainer/**`, `.envrc`
answers.why: A task that executes on folder open and pipes a remote script into a shell. The signal is what runs when the tree is opened.

answers.row: A dependency added recently, an unfamiliar maintainer, or a suspected incident
answers.why: A package published three days ago by a single-package account, with a borrowed README, arriving with a postinstall hook. The manifest row is always staffed and does not answer this.

answers.row: A payment, transfer or approval screen; biometric or PIN unlock; CodePush, Expo or other over-the-air updates
answers.why: An approval screen gated on a biometric callback and a bundle delivered over the air outside the store. No manifest and no Xcode project in the fragment.

answers.row: `.github/workflows/`
answers.why: `pull_request_target` with a checkout of the fork head and a publish token in the environment.

answers.row: Installer, self-update code, `autoUpdater`, a plugin directory loaded at runtime, a setuid binary, a service or daemon
answers.why: The Electron packaging is present, and the surface is the update channel: a feed served over plaintext HTTP that decides what code runs next.

answers.row: Signup, invitations, referrals, quotas, public enumeration surfaces
answers.why: A 409 that confirms an address is registered, and a referral credit written from a user-supplied identifier. Both are product decisions about abuse, not route defects.

answers.row: Branch and tag protection, `CODEOWNERS`, release tags, binaries tracked in the tree
answers.why: Ownership rules and an unreviewable binary the build already consumes.

answers.row: Admin panel, support impersonation, structured logging of user actions
answers.why: A staff-only impersonation route and a per-user export route. The staff check is present; the questions this row asks are what the acting principal may reach and what the record of it is worth.

answers.row: Outbound HTTP from user-controlled input, webhooks, URL fetching, previews
answers.why: A request parameter becomes the URL of a server-side fetch that follows redirects. The handler is an HTTP route, and the class is where the server is made to go.

answers.row: Vector store, embeddings, retrieval pipeline, ingestion job, agent memory
answers.why: An ingestion job reading a bucket into a vector column. What enters the index is content nobody in this tree wrote.

answers.row: Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, `kustomization.yaml`
answers.why: A templated chart, not rendered manifests. The values file is where the privileged and host-network settings actually resolve.

answers.row: `*.tf`, `*.tfvars`, CloudFormation, Bicep, Pulumi
answers.why: Infrastructure as code, with the public-access block written to allow rather than to block.

answers.row: Third-party SDKs, telemetry, tracking, ad libraries
answers.why: An analytics SDK with session replay and autocapture on, an email in the event payload, and a third-party pixel on the page.

answers.row: File upload, deserialization, template rendering, PDF/XML/YAML parsing
answers.why: An upload written to disk under a caller-supplied name and then parsed as XML.
